anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Row-count, histogram, and correlation metadata are stale, missing, or incomplete, causing systematic optimizer cardinality misestimation.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical pages or index structures are corrupted or inconsistent with logical data, making on-disk storage unreliable and leading to incorrect or missing rows.

When these two root causes coexist, the database exhibits a blend of cardinality-driven plan instability and corruption-driven data access failures: estimates diverge wildly from actual rows while index probes intermittently miss, duplicate, or corrupt result sets; the optimizer oscillates between inefficient full scans and reliance on damaged indexes; execution plans that appear optimal at compile time catastrophically underperform at run time; repeated recompilations, sudden "inaccurate page" or checksum errors, and alternating error codes for corruption and statistics invalidation are observed. Application symptoms range from severe latency spikes and deadlocks (due to unexpected scan types) to incorrect query results and aborted transactions.

Causally, corrupted data blocks distort row counts returned by sampling or validation routines, further polluting already stale statistics. In turn, bad statistics drive the optimizer to choose access paths (e.g., non-clustered index seeks) that intensify exposure to the very pages that are corrupt, multiplying read errors and forcing emergency fallbacks. Corruption can also prevent automatic statistics maintenance from scanning affected objects, letting staleness persist. The two anomalies therefore reinforce each other: corruption hides behind misestimation, and misestimation keeps the workload focused on corrupt structures, accelerating overall degradation of performance, reliability, and data accuracy.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
